about: Stages and settings for the governance review playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks and the outcomes each stage can record. The other keys are read by the assistant following SKILL.md. No stage waits for another: the whole review can run in one session. Each key is explained under notes.

owners.retention: project administrator and data protection lead

stages.name: access
stages.do: Review who has access to the Engagement projects in scope and add the removals, downgrades and confirmations as findings, grouped per project and never naming a person.

stages.name: integrations
stages.do: Inventory the project's integrations, API triggers, project variables and webhook steps, and add stored credentials, broken references and unused items as findings, never a secret.

stages.name: retention
stages.do: Compare event retention with the windows definitions read, and add breaks, over-kept data and personal properties as changes to consider. Not legal advice.

stages.name: datahub
stages.do: Audit the Data Hub workspace's item collections and add the high and medium fixes as findings with the owner the audit names. Record no_datahub when no workspace has Data Hub.

stages.name: ad-audiences
stages.do: Review the audiences sent to ad platforms and the autosegments, and add audiences without advertising consent, on archived segments, tiny, duplicated or failing as findings.

stages.name: catalog-exposure
stages.do: Audit the Discovery catalog's attribute settings and add internal fields returned to the storefront or facetable, and other high fixes, as findings.

stages.name: hidden-config
stages.do: Audit Discovery audiences and API parameter overrides, and add forgotten, broken or over-broad ones as findings.

notes.review_every_days: How often the review runs: about a quarter. The next run is a new hand-off file started this many days after the last one; step 0 lists the folder so the new run starts from the previous run's open findings.
notes.max_chosen: How many findings can be marked chosen at once: the ones the owners have agreed to act on this quarter. The review writes nothing, so chosen only means agreed; findings are marked done when the owner says the change is made.
notes.owners: Who usually acts on each stage's findings, by stage name. The playbook puts it in each finding's owner field (plain text: a team or role, never a person's name), and the summary groups the findings by owner. Override it with the owner the stage skill names on a row (datahub-collection-audit names one per fix) or the one the user gives.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes (none does here), what to do, the outcomes it can record and the product it needs: status suggests skipping the Engagement stages when the run has no Engagement project and the Discovery stages when it has no Discovery account. The datahub stage names no product: Data Hub sits under the cloud organisation, so a Discovery or an Engagement customer may have it, and the stage records no_datahub when no workspace has it. No skip_when entries: each audit stands alone, and one finding nothing doesn't make another pointless. The findings list with owners isn't a stage: no skill makes it, so the playbook builds it from the stages' findings.
